Question 12(c) [5 marks]: Analyse the impact of variation in demand and variety on this business.
STIMULUS / CASE INFORMATION:
Chris Cringle Decorations are a large Sydney based seller of artificial Christmas trees and decorations. They currently source stock from a Chinese manufacturer and storage costs have doubled within the last 6 months.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 5):
5 marks: Clearly identifies components and the relationship between variation in demand and variety for this business AND draws out and relates implications to the business
4 marks: Clearly identifies components and the relationship between variation in demand and variety for this business
3 marks: Identifies some components and the relationship between variation in demand and variety for this business
2 marks: Identifies some components OR relationship between variation in demand and variety for this business
1 marks: Makes a valid statement about variation in demand OR variety

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
Operations will be strongly influenced by variations in demand over time: demand can change according to time of day, season, public holidays and time of year. When demand is volatile, operations need to be highly flexible; the operations manager must anticipate and plan for changes in demand and keep a high level of contact with the market, using technology to respond quickly. Variety refers to the number of different models and variations offered. If customers have different needs, a wide variety of models and options will need to be provided, probably relying on sophisticated technology to change production from one product to another without too much disruption. A business offering high variety will be capital-intensive, with a focus on sourcing at the lowest cost per unit. However, due to the seasonal nature of CCD's products and the variation in demand, the business needs to be flexible about how much stock it holds during quiet months and manage both HR and facilities across the year to achieve efficiencies.
